summary.title: AgentDoG 1.5: A Lightweight and Scalable Alignment Framework for AI Agent Safety and Security

details: Open-world agents (OpenClaw/Codex-style) act across sessions, repositories, shells and MCP tools, creating trajectory-level risks that prompt- or output-level guardrails and fixed safety label sets cannot express or detect.
Existing guard models are large, coarse-grained (binary), and too costly to serve as verifiers/rewards inside agentic training or as low-latency runtime monitors.

AgentDoG 1.5: a family of tiny (0.8B-8B) trajectory-level diagnostic guardrail models that, given a full agent trajectory plus tool descriptions, emit a CoT rationale then a safe/unsafe verdict and a three-dimensional diagnosis (risk source, failure mode, real-world harm).

Crux of the recipe: a taxonomy-guided synthetic trajectory data engine with GPT-generated CoT rationales, then preference-aware influence-function purification that keeps only ~1k examples whose SFT gradients align with a guardrail 'identify-risk vs miss-risk' gradient direction, followed by SFT plus per-dimension-normalized RL (GDPO) on verifiable fine-grained labels.

Surrounding framework: an extensible three-dimensional safety taxonomy whose leaf categories are customized per execution setting, plus use of the guard model as an SFT data filter, an RL reward signal, and a Pre-Reply online guardrail.

ATBench family: base ATBench (1,000 trajectories, 503 safe/497 unsafe, 2,084 tools, ~9 turns each) plus new ATBench-Claw (500 trajectories, 204 safe/296 unsafe, ~13 events) and ATBench-Codex (500, 250/250, ~7.5 turns, ~21.8 rollout events); R-Judge for external trajectory judgment.

Taxonomy extension operations: add leaf categories (e.g., session-state contamination, approval bypass, repository artifact injection, dependency/MCP supply-chain compromise, destructive workspace mutation, unsafe shell execution) and sharpen inherited ones; a new compliance/auditability harm category.
Data pool for training covers 5,973 unique tools/MCP servers, 15 risk sources, 21 failure modes, 11 harm categories, with rule + model validation and soft class balancing.

Backbones: Qwen3.5-0.8B/2B/4B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; SFT lr 1e-5 on purified CoT data (~1k samples); RL with GDPO, per-dimension binary verifier rewards weighted (0.3,0.4,0.3), reasoning-block gate, clip 0.2/0.28, beta 0.001, lr 1e-6, G=8.
A bonus unified variant AgentDoG 1.5-4B-U jointly trained for coarse and fine-grained judgment; format-adaptation training for Codex/Claw trajectory schemas.
Open-source: Qwen3.5 (0.8B-397B-A17B), Qwen3-235B, QwQ-32B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B.
Guard models: LlamaGuard3/4, Qwen3-Guard, ShieldAgent, JoySafety, NemoGuard; plus AgentDoG 1.0-4B as prior version.

SFT data: ATBench engine produces 32,787 safety trajectory pairs; AgentDoG filtering retains 28,705, mixed ~1:2 with 50k benign tool-use trajectories from ToolBench/ToolAlpaca/ToolACE; Qwen3.5-4B fine-tuned (batch 128, 16k context, lr 5e-6).

RL: 15,222 tasks in LLM-generated finite-state Python simulators (323 tools, 16 domains) with injected environment-injection and malicious-query attacks; reward mixes rule-based utility U and AgentDoG safety score S; GSPO in Slime, 8 samples/task, batch 32, 400 steps, loss masking against format-collapse reward hacking.

Evaluation: AgentHarm (BS/HS/RR), AgentSafetyBench (SR), AgentSecurityBench (ASR), AgentDojo and AgentDyn (BU/UA/ASR), BFCL accuracy; ablations Util-only vs unfiltered-safe vs AgentDoG-filtered, and SFT vs RL vs SFT+RL.

Deployed on OpenClaw with GLM-5.1 backbone agent; proxy formats runtime events into a trajectory representation and AgentDoG judges the held final reply (greedy, max_tokens 1024, <Analysis>/<Judgment>).

Benchmarks: ClawSafety (16 financial-operation cases), AgentHazard Prompt Intelligence Theft (260), 35 retained CIK-Bench cases; metrics residual unsafe delivery ASR, TTFT, TPOT, completion tokens; compared with Qwen3Guard-Gen-4B and Llama-Guard-3-8B.

key_findings.finding: About 1k influence-purified, CoT-augmented taxonomy-guided samples suffice to make a 4B guard model match or beat frontier closed-source models on trajectory-level safety judgment and dominate them on fine-grained diagnosis.
key_findings.evidence: AgentDoG 1.5-4B reaches 92.2% Acc / 92.7 F1 on R-Judge and 72.4% Acc / 74.3 F1 on ATBench (vs Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 66.8/67.8 and GPT-5.4 73.7/76.7), and averages 55.2% on the three fine-grained dimensions versus 25.8% for GPT-5.4, 18.6% for Gemini-3.1-Pro and 34.6% for AgentDoG 1.0-4B (+20.6 points).

key_findings.finding: Using AgentDoG as a trajectory-level filter for safety SFT data yields better safety and less utility loss than training on the same unfiltered synthetic safety data.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen3.5-4B, filtered vs unfiltered safety data: AgentHarm harm score 20.32% vs 31.91%, refusal rate 75.00% vs 62.50%, AgentSecurityBench ASR 23.82% vs 34.72%, BFCL 81.12% vs 78.69% (base model: HS 57.49%, RR 28.41%, ASR 90.39%).

key_findings.finding: AgentDoG-guided RL on top of SFT recovers much of the benign utility lost to safety SFT while further improving safety, whereas RL alone is insufficient.
key_findings.evidence: SFT+RL attains the best AgentHarm refusal rate (77.27%) and AgentSafetyBench safe rate (59.32%) with BFCL 81.25%, raising AgentDojo benign utility from 42.53% (SFT-only) to 52.96%; RL-only reaches only 59.09% RR and 64.99% AgentSecurityBench ASR.

key_findings.finding: As a Pre-Reply runtime guardrail on OpenClaw, small AgentDoG models cut unsafe final deliveries where existing guard models fail, at sub-second first-token latency.
key_findings.evidence: ATBench-4B lowers ASR from 56.25% to 18.75% on ClawSafety, 41.92% to 26.92% on AgentHazard (Qwen3Guard and Llama-Guard both 0.00 delta there), and 94.29% to 42.86% on CIK-Bench, with TTFT means 0.17-0.30s and TPOT ~0.02s/token.
